shared_elements: frontal anthropomorphic figure with head at top and body below
low-relief carving on the stone surface
circular disc or medallion motif on the chest area
bilaterally symmetrical composition about a vertical axis
justification: Both are upright carved stone monuments organised symmetrically around a frontal figure whose broad headdress sits at the top, with a torso below bearing a prominent circular disc or medallion and horizontal banding — a genuinely comparable vertical scheme. They differ sharply in execution and form: A is a flat rectangular slab with crisp, densely detailed relief framed by columns of small block-like motifs, while B is a rounded boulder-like mass whose shallow, worn, almost schematic carving lacks any framing register or fine detail.
